author: Rahul kp
title: Composite vs
simple_words: If items naturally go together, tax follows the main item. If they are just packed together, tax follows the highest-taxed item.

definitions.meaning: A supply by a taxable person to a recipient of two or more taxable supplies that are naturally bundled and supplied together in the ordinary course of business, one being the principal supply.
Two or more individual supplies made together for a single price, which are not naturally bundled (not a composite supply). Single price alone does not make it mixed.

key_points: Section 8(a) CGST: ==composite supply== is taxed as the ==principal supply==.
Section 8(b) CGST: ==mixed supply== is taxed as the supply with the highest rate of tax.
Composite supply needs natural bundling in the ordinary course of business.
!!Single price is necessary for mixed supply, but it does not decide the type!!

insight.text: Ask first if the supplies are naturally bundled; only then look at the price and the tax treatment.

memory_trick.explanation: Naturally bundled goes with the Principal supply. Merely packed together takes the Peak (highest) rate.

steps: If yes: find the principal supply
If no: pick the highest-rate supply
exam_tip: Write the test in words: naturally bundled in the ordinary course of business. Then name Section 8(a) or 8(b).

doubt.question: Single price is there, so is it always mixed supply?
doubt.answer: No. A composite supply can also be at one price. Check natural bundling first; if it is bundled naturally, it is composite.

mistakes.wrong: Mixed supply is taxed at the principal supply rate
mistakes.right: Mixed supply is taxed as the supply with the highest rate of tax.

mistakes.wrong: Composite supply is taxed at the highest rate
mistakes.right: Composite supply is taxed as the principal supply.
Single price is necessary but not decisive; if naturally bundled, it is composite.

mistakes.wrong: Any combo sold together is composite
mistakes.right: It is composite only if naturally bundled in the ordinary course of business.

Checker 1: Steps 3–4 (and simple_words): 'If no: pick the highest-rate supply' skips the single-price test. Correct version: 'If not naturally bundled, check whether the supplies are made together for a single price. If yes, it is a mixed supply taxed at the highest rate (Section 8(b)). If no, tax each supply separately at its own rate.' simple_words should also say 'packed together for a single price', not 'just packed together'.

Checker 1: Mistake 3 right: 'Single price is necessary but not decisive' could be read as applying to composite supply too. Reword: 'A single price is a necessary condition only for mixed supply and is not decisive. A composite supply can also be at a single price. If the supplies are naturally bundled, it is composite.'

Checker 1: Definition 2 (Mixed supply): leaves out 'by a taxable person' and 'goods or services, or any combination thereof' from Section 2(74). Suggested wording: 'Two or more individual supplies of goods or services, or any combination thereof, made in conjunction with each other by a taxable person for a single price, where such supply does not constitute a composite supply.'
Checker 1: Definition 1 / key points: the note could cite the definition sections, Section 2(30) for composite supply and Section 2(74) for mixed supply, alongside Section 8.
